_about: Per-phase cheat sheet. Each entry's id is also its skill id in the skills table, so never change or reuse an id. aliases = exact inline-code texts that link to this entry; match = regex tested against inline code.

phase1.what: The MSVC compiler. Turns a .c file into an .exe, or stops and prints errors.
cd moves the terminal into a folder; dir lists what's in it. Be in your repo folder before compiling.
Pastes a header in before compiling, so you can use what it declares.
Where every C program starts. Its return value goes back to whatever ran it.
Prints text. % slots are filled, in order, by the values after the comma.
phase1.gotcha: Never adds a newline for you.

phase1.what: Escape sequences inside strings: newline, back to start of line, tab, one backslash.
%d is a whole-number slot in printf. %% prints one percent sign.
Ends main and tells the OS the program succeeded. Anything else means failure.
Ends every statement. A missing one is the most common first error.
An error stops the build. A warning (like C4244) builds anyway unless /WX turns it into an error.
A batch file holding your compile command, flags and files. Type build to run it.
Most warnings · warnings are errors · debug info (PDB) · no optimisation while developing.
The exit code of the last command. 0 means it worked; build.bat checks it.
Stage changes, save a labelled snapshot, send it to GitHub.
phase1.example:
git add .
git commit -m "feat: hello world"
git push

phase2.what: Whole numbers, about ±2.1 billion. Health, score, frame count.
Decimal numbers, ~7 digits. Positions, speed, timers. Write the f suffix.
Decimal with ~15 digits. Read with %lf in scanf.
One byte holding a character's ASCII number. Single quotes.
true or false. Needs #include <stdbool.h>. Prints as 1 or 0 with %d.
printf/scanf slots: float, char, float to 2 places, string. Must match the type.
Reads typed input into variables. Waits for Enter.
phase2.gotcha: The space before %c skips the leftover Enter. Returns how many values it read.

phase2.what: The address of a variable, so a function can write into it.
Runs the first block whose condition is true; the rest are skipped.
== compares and gives 1 or 0. = assigns and gives the assigned value.
phase2.gotcha: /W4 warns with C4706 inside a condition.

phase2.what: Repeat while the condition is true. For loops that wait for something to change.
Repeat a known number of times: start; keep going while; step.
A loop that always runs at least once. Good for "play, then ask again".
Picks a branch by value. Cleaner than many ifs for menus and states.
phase2.gotcha: Forget break and it falls into the next case.

phase2.what: int / int drops the fraction (7 / 2 is 3). % gives the remainder (7 % 2 is 1).
Converts a value on purpose. float → int truncates toward zero.
rand() gives a pseudo-random number; seed it once with srand(time(NULL)).
Size in bytes, worked out by the compiler. Returns size_t: cast before %d.

phase3.what: A named machine: inputs (parameters) in, one result (return value) out.
"Nothing": a function that returns no value, or takes no parameters.
A one-line promise that a function exists, so it can be called before its body.
Find-and-replace before compiling. Name your magic numbers.
A row of same-type boxes reached by index, starting at 0.
phase3.gotcha: Last index is size - 1; C won't stop you going past it.

phase3.what: The one loop shape for arrays. Never <= count.
How many elements an array has, where it was declared.
phase3.gotcha: Inside a function the array is a pointer; pass the count.

phase3.what: A char array that ends at the first '\0'. %s prints up to it.
The terminator byte, value 0. Not the digit '0' (48).
Reads a whole line safely: never writes past the size you give it.
phase3.gotcha: Keeps the Enter as '\n' — strip it.

phase3.what: Counts characters up to the '\0', not including it. Returns size_t.
Compares two strings. 0 means equal; only the sign of other results is guaranteed.
phase3.gotcha: if (strcmp(a, b)) runs when they're different.

phase3.what: An array of arrays — e.g. five names of up to 31 characters.
A variable declared inside { } only exists inside them, and is gone when the function returns.
phase3.example: void f(void) { int x = 1; }   // x is gone after this

phase3.what: Open a file, write or read it like printf/scanf, then close it.
phase3.gotcha: fopen returns NULL if it can't open. MSVC needs _CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS.

phase3b.what: Groups named fields of different types into one type.
The dot reaches a field when you hold the struct itself.
b = a copies every field. Passing a struct to a function copies it too.
phase3b.example: Player b = a;   // two separate players

phase3b.what: A variable that holds an address — where a value lives, not the value.
Dereference: go to the address in p and use what's there.
Address-of: the location of x. Hand it to functions that should change x.
Field through a pointer. Shorthand for (*p).health.
Functions that change an object take a pointer, so they change the real one.
phase3b.example: void player_move(Player* p, float dx, float dy);

phase3b.what: A pointer to nothing. Check for it before using a pointer.
.h declares what exists (types, prototypes). .c holds the bodies.
phase3b.example:
// player.h
void player_heal(Player* p, int amount);

phase3b.what: Top of a header: include this file only once per .c file.
phase3b.gotcha: Without it, a double include gives C2011.

phase3b.what: The compiler was happy but the body was never built — a .c file is missing from the build.
phase3b.example: cl main.c player.c   // list every .c file

phase3b.what: Breakpoint · run/continue · step over · step into. Watch panel shows live values.
phase3b.example: F9 on a line, F5, then F10 to step
phase3b.gotcha: Run build first — F5 launches the exe on disk.

phase3b.what: Named integer constants — perfect for game states.

phase4.what: Copy a repo to your machine; bring down your partner's new commits.
A separate line of work. main stays buildable; features live on branches.
Ask to merge a branch into main, with a review first.
Two changes to the same lines. Git marks both; you pick, delete the markers, commit.
Files Git should never track: build output like .exe, .obj, .pdb.
type: short description — feat, fix, refactor, docs.

phase4b.what: Is a key waiting? (never waits) / take that key (no Enter, no echo).
Gives the CPU back for at least ms milliseconds. From <windows.h>.
phase4b.gotcha: At least, never exactly — about 15.6 ms granularity.

phase4b.what: Print a whole frame starting with \r and no \n: it paints over the last one.
Push buffered output to the screen now. Needed when a line has no \n.
Build the whole frame in memory, then show it in one go. No flicker.
An enum for the current state and one switch that does that state's work.
A value meaning "empty", so a fixed array can be reused instead of allocating.
The four steps every frame of every game.
A read-only pointer: the function promises not to change what it points at.
A body or variable in a header got included into two .c files.
phase4b.example:
// runner.h: declarations only
void runner_reset(Runner* r);

phase5.what: The starting point of a Windows GUI program, instead of main.
phase5.example: int WINAPI WinMain(HINSTANCE h, HINSTANCE p, LPSTR cmd, int show)

phase5.what: A handle — an ID number — for one window.
Collect Windows' messages (keys, clicks, close) and hand each to your WndProc.
Like GetMessage but never waits — lets a game loop keep running.
Your function Windows calls with each message: WM_KEYDOWN, WM_PAINT, WM_DESTROY…
Tells Windows part of the window needs repainting (sends WM_PAINT).
Windows libraries that hold the window and drawing functions. Link them.
Measure how long each frame really took, instead of trusting Sleep.
Draw to an off-screen bitmap, then copy it to the window in one go.

phase6.what: Seconds since last frame. Multiply speeds by it so movement is the same at any fps.
phase6.example: x += speed * dt;   // speed in pixels/second

phase6.what: Two axis-aligned boxes overlap if they overlap on x and on y.
phase6.example:
a.x < b.x + b.w && a.x + a.w > b.x &&
a.y < b.y + b.h && a.y + a.h > b.y

phase6.what: Change state once, at the end of the frame, so no code runs twice.
Update changes the game; render only draws it. Pause = skip update, keep render.
GDI functions that draw text in the window — for the score.
